Find all values of $k$ for which the system
\begin{align*}
x + ky - z &= 0, \\
kx - y - z &= 0, \\
x + y - kz &= 0
\end{align*}has a non-trivial solution.  (In other words, find all values of $k$ for which the system has a solution other than $(x,y,z) = (0,0,0).$)
oczekiwana_odpowiedz:
We can write the system as
\[\begin{pmatrix} 1 & k & -1 \\ k & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -k \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}.\]This system has a nontrivial system exactly when the determinant of the matrix is 0.  This determinant is
\begin{align*}
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & k & -1 \\ k & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -k \end{pmatrix} &= \begin{vmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -k \end{vmatrix} - k \begin{vmatrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & -k \end{vmatrix} + (-1) \begin{vmatrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \\
&= ((-1)(-k) - (-1)(1)) - k((k)(-k) - (-1)(1)) - ((k)(1) - (-1)(1)) \\
&= k^3 - k.
\end{align*}The solutions to $k^3 - k = k(k - 1)(k + 1) = 0$ are $\boxed{-1,0,1}.$

The system is:
\begin{align*}
1x + ky - 1z &= 0 \\
kx - 1y - 1z &= 0 \\
1x + 1y - kz &= 0
\end{align*}

The coefficient matrix $A$ is:
$$A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & k & -1 \\ k & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & -k \end{pmatrix}$$

We calculate the determinant of $A$, denoted as $\det(A)$:
$$\det(A) = 1 \begin{vmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -k \end{vmatrix} - k \begin{vmatrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & -k \end{vmatrix} + (-1) \begin{vmatrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$$

Calculate each $2 \times 2$ determinant:
1. $\begin{vmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -k \end{vmatrix} = (-1)(-k) - (-1)(1) = k + 1$
2. $\begin{vmatrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & -k \end{vmatrix} = (k)(-k) - (-1)(1) = -k^2 + 1$
3. $\begin{vmatrix} k & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = (k)(1) - (-1)(1) = k + 1$

Substitute these back into the determinant expression:
$$\det(A) = 1(k + 1) - k(-k^2 + 1) - 1(k + 1)$$
$$\det(A) = k + 1 + k^3 - k - k - 1$$
$$\det(A) = k^3 - k$$

For the system to have a non-trivial solution, we must have $\det(A) = 0$:
$$k^3 - k = 0$$
$$k(k^2 - 1) = 0$$
$$k(k - 1)(k + 1) = 0$$

The solutions for $k$ are $k = 0$, $k = 1$, and $k = -1$.

We can verify these values:
- If $k=0$: The equations are $x-z=0, -y-z=0, x+y=0$. This gives $x=z, y=-z$, so $(z, -z, z)$ is a solution.
- If $k=1$: The equations are $x+y-z=0, x-y-z=0, x+y-z=0$. This gives $y=0$ and $x=z$, so $(z, 0, z)$ is a solution.
- If $k=-1$: The equations are $x-y-z=0, -x-y-z=0, x+y+z=0$. Adding the first two gives $-2y-2z=0 \Rightarrow y=-z$. Then $x-(-z)-z=0 \Rightarrow x=0$. So $(0, -z, z)$ is a solution.

The values of $k$ are $0, 1, -1$.
